# What the simulation says about the parameters

*Generated by `node lab/search-v2/tools/simulate.mjs` — 20 simulated participants, 10 on sequence A and 10 on B, each playing all 28 rounds of the real frozen artifacts under five policies. Every number below is from that run; nothing is asserted that the simulator did not measure.*

## The short answer

The environment is well posed and the costs are in the right relation to each other, but
**the design as it stands does not deliver the sparse/dense sign flip it predicts**, and one
parameter — the reveal cap — is doing more work than it was meant to. The specifics:

## 1 · Reveal 5 and question 2 — adequate, and the ratio is the load-bearing part

The costs are what make the two search styles cost different amounts, and they do separate:

| | mean score | questions | reveals | total spent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rational, no AI | 64.04 | 0.00 | 1.86 | 9.31 |
| rational, with AI | 57.63 | 12.92 | 0.23 | 27.00 |
| trusting | 69.93 | 4.16 | 0.49 | 10.76 |

With the best prize on the board averaging 94.8 points, an unaided
rational search spends 9.31 of it on reveals — a little over 10% of the prize. That is high enough for the search to bite and low enough that a round is
rarely negative, which is the band the design wants. **No change recommended.**

## 2 · K = 4 and K = 10 — the sparse side works, the dense side is the problem

The design predicts a SIGN FLIP because the sparse mid-gap standard deviation, 14.43, sits above
s\* = 12.53 and the dense one, 9.13, sits below it. What the simulation finds:

| policy | sparse effect | dense effect | sparse − dense | flip? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RATIONAL-NO-AI | -0.50 | +0.47 | -0.97 | no — gradient |
| RATIONAL-WITH-AI | -7.78 | -4.89 | -2.89 | no — gradient |
| TRUSTING | +3.77 | +7.96 | -4.19 | no — gradient |
| SKEPTICAL | +0.28 | -1.42 | +1.69 | no — gradient |
| NOISY-SATISFICER | +0.78 | +1.89 | -1.12 | no — gradient |

## 3 · The caps (40 questions / 20 reveals)

Mean reveals per round never approaches 40 questions; the binding constraint is the reveal
cap. Unaided rational search uses 1.86 reveals of the 20 allowed.

## 6 · The null check

`RATIONAL-NO-AI` ignores the condition entirely, so its crossover effect is the
simulator's own zero: **-0.01 points** with a paired sd of 3.45. Any effect
below that magnitude is spec heterogeneity between the two blocks, not the AI.
